articles.headline: Antonelli takes surprise pole to boost chances of sealing title in USA
keyFacts: Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to take pole position for the United States Grand Prix in Austin.
Antonelli could secure his maiden Formula 1 world championship on Sunday if he wins the race and other results favor him.
Isack Hadjar qualified third for Red Bull, while Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton took fourth and fifth.
body: United States GP Qualifying: Kimi Antonelli beats Max Verstappen to surprise pole to boost chances of sealing maiden F1 title on Sunday

Kimi Antonelli stuns Max Verstappen to take pole in Austin; Antonelli could be crowned world champion on Sunday if he wins and other results go his way; watch the United States GP live on Sky Sports F1 & Sky Sports Main Event at 8pm on Sunday, with build-up from 6.30pm
Saturday 24 October 2026 23:26, UK
Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the United States Grand Prix to boost his chances of sealing a maiden world championship in Sunday's race.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver is all but certain to become Formula 1's youngest ever champion but could clinch the title with five rounds to spare if he wins in Austin on Sunday and other placings go his way.

It was perhaps the most unlikely of Antonelli's seven poles this season as he came from nowhere in Q3 to surge ahead of Verstappen, who had appeared for most of the weekend to be battling Ferrari for the front-row positions.
Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar equalled his best qualifying result by taking third, leaving Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton fourth and fifth, respectively.

George Russell will start from sixth, with the Brit needing to finish in the top eight to ensure Antonelli won't be crowned champion if he wins on Sunday. Hamilton would also need to finish fifth or lower in the event of an Antonelli victory for the title to be confirmed.
Oscar Piastri took seventh ahead of his McLaren team-mate Lando Norris as the latter was demoted from sixth after having his final effort deleted for breaching track limits.
Racing Bulls took the final two top-10 places but Liam Lawson will inherit ninth from his team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine component allowance.

articles.headline: Chelsea sweat over Joao Pedro injury after missing Tottenham defeat
keyFacts: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro missed the match against Tottenham after picking up a knee injury in training on Friday.
Manager Xabi Alonso stated that further medical tests are required once fluid buildup subsides to determine the injury severity.
Alonso also confirmed that goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez will be out for several weeks following surgery for a fractured jaw.
body: Joao Pedro was left out of Chelsea ’s squad for their London derby defeat to Tottenham and requires further assessment after picking up an injury in training on Friday.

The striker, who has scored five goals and made three assists in the Premier League this season, suffered a knee injury which ruled him out of Chelsea’s match with Brentford ahead of the September international break, and he withdrew from Brazil duty.

He returned to the Chelsea team to score twice against Bournemouth and then played 90 minutes against Everton last weekend. But Pedro is not involved for the clash with Spurs due to another fitness issue, which is being assessed by the club.

Manager Xabi Alonso told Sky Sports : “Yesterday in training he felt something, and at the moment he has some liquid, so we have to do some tests to know how big the injury is. It's disappointing, but we need to carry on.”
Chelsea went on to suffer their first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018 with Joao Pedro’s absence being felt up front, losing 2-0 following a late capitulation.

Speaking more on Pedro’s status after the match, Alonso added: “We don't know yet because he has a lot of fluid, so he felt it yesterday and we need to wait probably until tomorrow to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury and we will know soon enough.”

Alonso made no mention of Pedro’s fitness during his pre-match press conference, but did confirm that Argentinian goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ​will be out for several weeks after surgery on a fractured jaw, which brings Mike Penders into the side.
Martinez ​was ⁠taken to hospital following a collision with defender Jarrad Branthwaite during last weekend’s 2-0 win over Everton.
“He’s been better; ⁠he had the surgery. We still ​need ⁠to wait. (He will be ‌out for] a few weeks. Hopefully less than more,” Alonso told a press ‌conference on Friday.

articles.headline: NC State fires Dave Doeren: Wolfpack coach out amid 14th season after brutal loss to Stanford
keyFacts: NC State fired head coach Dave Doeren after 14 seasons, following a 31-28 loss to Stanford and a 3-4 start to the 2026 season.
Athletic director Boo Corrigan announced the decision on Saturday, thanking Doeren for his service and leadership during his tenure.
NC State will now begin its first football coaching search since 2012, after Doeren finished with a 98-73 overall record.
body: NC State has fired coach Dave Doeren after 14 seasons, the program announced on Saturday. The news comes one day after the Wolfpack lost 31-28 to Stanford on Friday.

"I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," NC State athletic director Boo Corrigan said. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role. We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future."

The Wolfpack are off to a disappointing 3-4 start in 2026. Outside of an upset victory against Louisville, NC State is 0-4 against Power Four opponents. Against lowly Stanford, NC State allowed 303 yards and four touchdowns to Cardinal quarterback Davis Warren, part of a 477-yard day.

Doeren was the model of consistency for most of his tenure, posting 10 winning seasons and 11 bowl appearances in the last 12 seasons. He led NC State to four nine-win seasons, each tied for the second-best mark in program history.

However, NC State never quite got over the top under Doeren's leadership, leaving the late Chuck Amato's 2002 squad with Philip Rivers as the only 10-win team in school history. And as the NIL era got underway, Doeren struggled to keep the program moving forward.

Last season showed promise during an 8-5 season headlined by breakout quarterback CJ Bailey. The Wolfpack invested heavily to retain Bailey, but lost running back Hollywood Smothers (Texas), wide receiver Noah Rogers (Alabama), offensive tackle Jacarrius Peak (South Carolina) and wide receiver Terrell Anderson (USC).
Now, NC State is set to embark on its first coaching search since 2012. Doeren finishes his tenure with a 98-73 mark and a 52-57 record in ACC play.

articles.headline: Barack Obama to rally for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan before key US Senate race – US politics live
keyFacts: Former president Barack Obama rallied in Detroit to support Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
The rally coincided with the start of Michigan's in-person early voting period ten days before election day.
Donald Trump is scheduled to visit Michigan tomorrow, followed by a visit from JD Vance later this week.
body: Obama to rally for El-Sayed in Detroit ahead of key US Senate race
Good afternoon and welcome to a rare weekend edition of the Guardian’s US politics live blog.
We are coming to you live as US midterm elections draw closer and candidates are jockeying fiercely to win the hearts, minds and votes of the American people.

As part of progressive Abdul El-Sayed’s effort to do just that, he’s added Democratic star power to his rally lineup tonight in Detroit: former president Barack Obama will take the stage and offer his support to the Senate hopeful.
This rally falls on the first day of Michigan’s in-person early voting period and 10 days before election day.
Stick with us as we bring you the latest news from the rally and beyond.

Rally goers in Michigan are now waiting for Abdul El-Sayed and Barack Obama to arrive at the venue in Detroit, where state candidates including senator Elissa Slotkin and US House candidate Christina Hines have already spoken.
Jocelyn Benson, the current secretary of state who’s running to be the state’s next governor, has just begun speaking – suggesting El-Sayed and Obama may not be far behind.

As of Friday afternoon, more than 23 million Americans had already voted in person or by mail. Among the key battleground states, Michigan and Ohio have each passed 900,000 ballots cast, while Georgia has recorded almost 1.5m early votes, North Carolina more than 1.2m, Florida almost 2.2m and Texas more than 2.8m, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab, as of 23 October.
2. Those early votes are pacing well ahead of 2022
Early voting is soaring compared with the last midterms in many of the battleground states, which will decide control of the Senate.
3. Democrats lead in early returns

Registered Democrats account for 45% of early ballots cast, compared with 30% from Republicans (tracking returned ballots, not candidate selection). The party gap is particularly pronounced in North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa – all states that traditionally favor Republicans.
Trump votes in midterm elections from West Palm Beach, Florida

Donald Trump voted in West Palm Beach, Florida today, telling reporters at the polls that he voted straight Republican on his ballot. Trump has historically mailed-in his ballot rather than voting in-person.

Speaking from the polling site, Trump defended an ad from Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, his administration’s lawsuit seeking to block certification of the Alaska Senate race if Repubican senator Dan Sullivan loses his race and the war in Iran.

The man who recently attempted to ambush the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a question about his supposed allegiance to the Muslim Brotherhood – which El-Sayed parlayed into a viral clip for his campaign – is the son of a political operator who recently received $250,000 for “canvassing and influencer marketing” against El-Sayed, the Guardian has learned.

In the now-famous exchange, a man – first identified by the Handbasket as Thomas “Tommy” Teepell – asked El-Sayed if he would “disavow” the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said he would, but then asked: “What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?” What followed was a five-minute exchange that has drawn over 50m views across several social media platforms, in which El-Sayed queries the man about the guarantees of religious freedom in the constitution.

Teepell is the son of Timothy “Timmy” Teepell, a longtime strategist for the Missouri Republican senator Josh Hawley as well as former Republican Louisiana governor Bobby Jindal. Timmy Teepell’s firm, Breakthrough LLC, was paid $250,000 on 29 September by America Next, a 501(c)(4) non-profit with which it shares a Baton Rouge office suite, according to a filing with the Federal Election Commission (FEC).
The El-Sayed rally in Michigan is under way with members of the state’s Democratic party speaking in advance of Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed and former president Barack Obama.
Speaking after House of Representatives candidate Christina Hines, current senator Elissa Slotkin said, “When Barack Obama comes to Detroit, Democrats win.”
Slotkin noted that the Obama’s visit was well timed, with Donald Trump expected to visit Michigan tomorrow, and JD Vance visiting later this week.
Trump continues his midterms campaign blitz in Georgia
While Barack Obama and Abdul El-Sayed have Democrats’ attention locked on Michigan today, Donald Trump is slated to speak today in Georgia.
The president is expected to announce that the car company Audi will build a new plant there, which is expected to produce 200,000 SUVs annually, Reuters reports.
My colleague Joseph Gedeon is attending the rally for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan today, where he says thousands are in attendance. Joseph will bring us the latest lines directly from the rally.
Analysis: El-Sayed confronts critics head-on as attacks ramp up
Joseph Gedeon

As a candidate positioned at the center of what researchers say are the worst Islamophobic attacks seen since the aftermath of 9/11, many would expect Abdul El-Sayed to simply defend himself and move on.

Instead, the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan has repeatedly demanded those who question his positions on Israel, the Muslim Brotherhood and his faith, explain the premise of their inquiry. Rather than let others put his loyalties on trial, he has tried to put their assumptions on trial.

The clearest example is a town hall exchange from last weekend that has been viewed more than 50m times. A man in the crowd demanded he disavow the Muslim Brotherhood. “Sure, yeah, absolutely,” El-Sayed said. Then: “What are you implying? Do you assume that I wouldn’t?”

His direct approach has yielded a nickname: “Mean Mamdani”, or “Meandami”. While New York City mayor and fellow Muslim Zohran Mamdani wins people over with warmth, El-Sayed goes at his critics head-on. Both have made establishment resistance part of their political identity, but El-Sayed treats confrontation itself as a way to expose what he sees as a rigged political debate.
It is an approach the Democratic establishment doesn’t quite know what to do with.

Barack Obama made his first appearance of the 2026 midterms campaign season today at an earlier event in Cleveland. There, the former president stumped for the Democratic Senate nominee, Sherrod Brown, and gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton.
In Cleveland, Obama sharply criticized Donald Trump, and a recent ad the state’s Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy released in recent days.
“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in modern times, you get a chance to say enough is enough,” Obama said.

He added that it seemed there was “no line” Ramaswamy was not willing to cross after releasing an ad featuring Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing the daughter she lost custody of in 1978, after her second husband was charged with raping her then 12-year-old daughter, of lying about her childhood.
Abdul El-Sayed, a doctor and former Wayne county health director, ran on Medicare for All and a refusal to take corporate Pac money, and was backed by Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
Barack Obama’s presence matters most in Detroit, where Black residents make up more than three-quarters of the population and where he is still highly popular.
Kamala Harris, the first Black and south Asian vice-president, campaigned with El-Sayed last month, and Obama phoned him after the primary.
Hundreds of people wait to see Obama at El-Sayed rally

Hundreds of Michiganders have gathered outside Cass Technical High School in Detroit, Michigan, where former president Barack Obama will stump for Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at a rally slated to begin in about an hour.

articles.headline: Johnny Depp's 96-Minute Stephen King Thriller Is an Underrated Gem on Streaming
keyFacts: The 2004 Stephen King thriller Secret Window, starring Johnny Depp, is currently ranking No. 4 on HBO Max's movie chart according to FlixPatrol.
The film follows a struggling writer at a secluded home who is accused of plagiarism by a mysterious and threatening stranger.
Secret Window holds a 46 percent critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes and features performances by Johnny Depp and John Turturro.
body: Stephen King has spent decades turning our worst nightmares into some of Hollywood's most memorable horror movies. From supernatural terror to small-town nightmares, the author's work continues to inspire filmmakers, with a fresh wave of adaptations bringing his stories to new audiences.

The latest Carrie adaptation has already been renewed for a second season after earning rave reviews, while The Long Walk brought King's brutal dystopian story to theaters in 2025. Mike Flanagan is also still developing a television adaptation of The Dark Tower, and Netflix has plans to revisit Cujo, proving that Hollywood isn't running out of King stories to take to the screen.

But while the author's most recognizable works continue to attract attention, some of his lesser-known stories have slipped under the radar. One 2004 adaptation that explores paranoia, isolation, and the frightening possibility that you can't trust your own mind is suddenly finding a new audience on streaming.

That is Secret Window, the 2004 thriller starring Johnny Depp. Based on King's novella Secret Window, Secret Garden, the film follows a troubled writer whose quiet retreat becomes increasingly disturbing when a stranger accuses him of stealing a story. It's currently ranking No. 4 on HBO Max's movie chart, according to FlixPatrol, giving this overlooked King adaptation another moment in the spotlight.
What Is Secret Window About?

Directed and written by David Koepp (Stir of Echoes, Panic Room), Secret Window stars Depp as Mort Rainey, a successful writer struggling through a bitter divorce. Seeking some peace, Mort retreats to his secluded lakeside home in upstate New York, hoping to put his personal troubles behind him and get back to writing.

His solitude doesn't last long. A mysterious man named John Shooter (John Turturro) arrives at his door, accusing Mort of plagiarizing one of his short stories. Mort initially dismisses the accusation, but Shooter grows increasingly threatening as he demands justice for the alleged theft.

As the confrontation escalates and disturbing incidents begin to pile up, Mort struggles to establish what is really happening around him. Unlike King's more creature-driven adaptations, Secret Window builds its horror around psychological tension. Its remote setting, increasingly erratic protagonist, and growing sense of paranoia create a story in which the line between reality and delusion is harder to distinguish.

Although Secret Window has developed a following among Stephen King fans, its critical reception has been more mixed than that of the author's most celebrated adaptations. The film holds a 46% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, compared with a 65% audience score, with critics praising Johnny Depp's quirky performance while arguing that the story loses momentum toward the end.

Still, mixed reviews haven't stopped Secret Window from appealing to viewers drawn to psychological thrillers. Depp brings an increasingly unsettled energy to writer Mort Rainey, while John Turturro makes for an unnerving adversary. It may not rank among King's most acclaimed adaptations, but its atmosphere of paranoia and escalating dread offers a welcome alternative to the supernatural horror stories that often dominate his screen legacy.

articles.headline: Intelligence chief Jay Clayton warns Rubio of rising Iranian threats
keyFacts: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian plans to kill U.S. citizens abroad reached advanced stages.
The State Department reduced diplomatic staffing at several Middle Eastern embassies and updated travel advisories following Iranian and Houthi threat escalations.
President Donald Trump suggested the U.S. could escalate military attacks against Iran if the country refuses to agree to a peace deal.
body: The head of U.S. intelligence warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday that Iranian plans to target and kill U.S. citizens abroad have reached “advanced stages.”

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent a memo alerting that “lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages” in the Middle East and other countries. Iran has “substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel” abroad, the DNI chief said, adding that the risk is “relevant to more individuals than are currently cleared to receive this information.”

“We will make every effort to downgrade as much intelligence as possible so you can share it with State Department personnel at your discretion,” Clayton told Rubio in the unclassified memo, on which CIA Director John Ratcliffe was also copied.

The development follows Iran’s threats to intensify attacks against the U.S. should President Donald Trump decide to renew his war in earnest against the country. During a rally for Byron Donalds (R-FL) on Friday, the president suggested he is considering launching another “Epic Fury” campaign against Iran, referring to the military operation Washington authorized against the country in February.

Clayton’s warning also comes after the State Department withdrew most staff from its embassy in Saudi Arabia earlier this week, in response to missile attacks Iran-backed Houthi terrorists operating in Yemen launched toward the country. Earlier this month, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid Airport killed at least twelve people, including a U.S. citizen, and injured hundreds more.

Rubio has adjusted diplomatic staffing at several other embassies in the region, as Iran maintains its grip on terrorist proxy groups across the Middle East . On Saturday, the State Department updated travel advisories for more than a dozen countries across the Gulf and Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United ​Arab Emirates, Iraq and ​Israel, citing an increased ⁠threat from Iran-aligned Houthis, according to Reuters .

“The threat ​of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting US officials are ​informing our ⁠decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO Status in the region,” a U.S. official said, referring to the Restricted Operations Status that provides the State Department more flexibility in personnel decisions without having to publicly alert to a change ⁠in the ​status of a mission.

The State Department ordered a further reduction in staff at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to NBC News, after announcing Wednesday that the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia would operate only with emergency staff, in response to intensified attacks by the Houthis.
TRUMP’S $5,000 CHECK PROMISE FACES MAJOR OBSTACLES

As Iran and its proxies remain on the loose, Trump suggested at a campaign rally in Florida on Friday that the U.S. could escalate military attacks against Tehran if it refuses to agree to a peace deal.
Iran has pushed back on such rhetoric.

“Any further escalation around the Strait of Hormuz or elsewhere in the region will put civilian lives and the well-being of all regional states and the global economy at great risk,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote in an opinion column in the Financial Times this week.

articles.headline: United States Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli takes pole – live
keyFacts: Kimi Antonelli secured pole position for the United States Grand Prix with a time of 1:34.035.
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff stated that winning the title tomorrow is not realistic, focusing instead on constructors' points.
Antonelli stated his intention to try to win the race and lead into turn one, while noting Max Verstappen's speed.
body: “We’re not talking about that … it’s not realistic,” Wolff says about Antonelli winning the title tomorrow. It’s all abiut getting points for the constructors’ championship, apparently. What’s the Austrian-German idiom for pull the other one?
Wolff addresses Russell’s situation, “an absolutely world-class driver”. Basically the car is there, and Russell needs to point himself in the right direction.

Jenson Button talks of Antonelli’s emotion at taking pole. Wolff says: “We know how important it is to find out what went wrong with the upgrade … and now we see that the car is there.” This all bodes well for 2027.

It’s very much possible. Antonelli’s first pole for eight races has come at the perfect time. Naomi Schiff is trying to work out the percentage chances of him winning this weekend, saying that the Sky panel were saying it was 4-5% pre-qualifying.

And here is Kimi. “We’ve got pole so we’ll try to win … but Max has been very quick. We’ll try to lead into turn one.” Again he references the wind. So that seems to be part of the explanation for what we saw generally, but what will Ferrari say?
Maybe I should give up on the prediction game. If Antonelli is to be champion this weekend then he has got just what he needed. A strange Q3, with little improvement and Ferrari dropping away.
The man-boy who would be king has that pole position, in 1:34.035! Verstappen, Hadjar, Leclerc, Hamilton, Russell, Piastri, Norris – his fastest lap time deleted – Lindblad and Lawson.
Everyone in the pits. Liam Lawson is sitting this sesssion out, saving tyres: he can’t crack the top eight and a penalty means he will be ahead of his teammate Lindblad.
Norris breaks things up, second fastest by 0.068. Antonelli third at +0.285, followed by Russell in +0.309. Russell was complaining earlier that he was rather too literally in the hot seat.
Anthony Davidson looking at Williams’s problems. They are faster on the straights than Ferrari but being massacred at the corners. A very disappointing 2026.
A word, though, for Liam Lawson. He is running seventh at +0.462. He has thoroughly justified his place this season after his abrupt demotion last year.

articles.headline: Why did NC State fire Dave Doeren? Wolfpack make change in wake of loss to Stanford
keyFacts: NC State fired head coach Dave Doeren on Saturday following a 31-28 loss to Stanford.
Athletic director Boo Corrigan thanked Doeren for his 14-year tenure and leadership since 2013.
Special teams and running backs coach Todd Goebbel will take over the team on an interim basis.
body: NC State lost 31-28 to Stanford on Friday night, a result that was apparently enough for the Wolfpack to make a coaching change.

Less than 24 hours after the result, NC State announced it fired long-time head coach Dave Doeren amid the 3-4 season. Doeren was one of the longest-tenured head coaches in the country, as he had been in Raleigh since the 2013 season.

In Doeren's spot, special teams and running backs coach Todd Goebbel will take over the team on an interim basis. Goebbel has been at NC State since 2019 and has never been a head coach in any capacity.
NEWS: NC State has fired head coach Dave Doeren. Wolfpack lost to Stanford last night.
— Chris Vannini (@ChrisVannini) October 24, 2026
Here's more on why NC State fired Doeren.
MORE: Malachi Toney makes case for top college wide receiver
Why did NC State fire Dave Doeren?

NC State fired Doeren on Saturday following a loss to Stanford on Friday night, marking the Wolfpack's fourth of the season. That puts NC State just one loss away from matching its total from all of 2025, yet the team is still five wins away from reaching last year's eight-win mark.

"I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," AD Boo Corrigan said. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role."

Doeren had been at NC State since 2013, producing losing seasons just three times but never reaching 10 wins in any season. The Wolfpack seemingly decided that it was time to move on from Doeren after over a decade of similar results.

articles.headline: Customizable split mechanical keyboard with integrated central touchpad goes on preorder for $160 — and this 3-pound slab is wireless and doesn't come with an infamous Copilot key
keyFacts: Vantex introduced the V1, a split mechanical keyboard featuring a central touchpad and priced starting at $129 for wired packages and $159 for wireless packages on Kickstarter.
Vantex stated that the wireless version is still in development, meaning its battery life and connection performance are currently being evaluated.
The Kickstarter campaign has raised $2,556 from 19 backers, surpassing its funding goal with 27 days remaining.
body: - Vantex V1 central touchpad eliminates the need to reach for a separate mouse
- Vantex offers wired and wireless packages starting at $129 and $159, respectively
- The V1 has 60 keys, four programmable layers, and an aluminium body
Vantex has introduced the V1, a mechanical keyboard incorporating a central touchpad that lets users control their computer without reaching for a separate mouse.
The keyboard measures 30.74 × 13.74 × 3.48 cm, weighs approximately 1.57 kg, and has a rearward incline of 7°.
This device packs 60 keys and four programmable layers into a CNC-machined aluminium body with a durable powder-coated finish, designed for office keyboard users.
A split keyboard with integrated navigation
The V1 uses a split key arrangement, leaving space between both sections for a 45 × 45 mm touch-sensitive surface for cursor movement.
Users can switch between typing and pointing without moving their hands far from the keyboard.
Vantex says its wired prototype has undergone testing with Windows, macOS and Linux, while connectivity options include USB-C, Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz wireless.
The wireless model has a 4,000 mAh battery, but its operating duration and connection performance remain under evaluation.

Its mechanical switches support replacement without soldering, while a gasket-mounted construction cushions keystrokes, offering features that may interest gaming keyboard enthusiasts.
The PBT keycaps use dye sublimation printing, and their layouts can be customized using an included interchangeable keycap collection.
This device comes with white linear switches that have an actuation force of 42 ± 3 gf, a bottom-out force of 47 ± 5 gf, and a stated lifespan of 50 million keystrokes
Early pledges offer discounts before production
The Kickstarter campaign lists an introductory price of $129 for the wired package, about 50% off the regular price of $259.
That package includes the keyboard without fitted keycaps, 148 keycaps and a data cable, requiring buyers to install their preferred arrangement themselves.
A two-keyboard wired bundle costs $239, against a listed retail price of $518, while the wireless package starts at $159.
Buyers seeking wireless connectivity can select a two-keyboard bundle priced at $299, which is 50% off the advertised standard price of $598.
The wireless version is still in development, so its real-world performance can’t be guaranteed, and backers should weigh that risk before pledging.
Unlike many newer Windows keyboards, the Vantex V1 does not include Microsoft's dedicated Copilot key.
This omission may appeal to users who prefer conventional keyboard controls without a dedicated button for launching Microsoft's AI assistant.
According to Vantex, it is still evaluating battery capacity, runtime, and connectivity for wireless operation.
The company has identified component availability, assembly consistency, final testing, packaging and international shipping as potential sources of production delays.
Vantex also discloses using AI-assisted tools for promotional writing, visual design and image enhancement, suggesting that the campaign materials may not represent the actual product.
At the time of writing, the Vantex V1 Kickstarter campaign has raised $2,556 from 19 backers, exceeding its $637 funding goal with 27 days remaining before it closes.

articles.headline: Xbox Reportedly Bungled $500 Million Netflix Exclusivity Deal To Develop Movies, Shows Based On Games
keyFacts: Puck News reported that Netflix offered Xbox $500 million for a seven-year exclusive deal to adapt its gaming intellectual property.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly countered with $800 million, causing Netflix to rescind the offer, according to the report.
Xbox stated that Netflix remains a valued partner and reported receiving record-breaking interest in adapting its properties.
body: While the video game industry seems to be in free fall, especially at Xbox, the TV-pulled-from-video-games industry is on the rise. Especially at Xbox. Earlier this month, Microsoft announced a new department dedicated to cross-media property development. According to an industry insider, the team may have come from the ashes of a burned deal with Netflix, after Xbox reportedly over-leveraged the value of its intellectual properties.

In a report from Puck News‘ Matthew Belloni, a deal was forming between Xbox and Netflix to develop projects based on its extensive gaming portfolio. In a write-up on freshly arrived Netflix executive Peter Rice, it was revealed that the streaming megalith offered newly appointed Xbox CEO Asha Sharma $500 million for exclusive rights to adapt a great deal of their intellectual property over a seven year period. A shiny figure. A healthy chunk of time. But Sharma apparently upped the ante to $800 million, at which point Netflix rescinded the offer.

In a statement to Puck, Xbox says that “Netflix is a valued partner,” and that on top of upcoming animated Minecraft and Diablo series they have “received record-breaking interest” in adapting their IP. Belloni writes that in response to the failed wager, Xbox is seeking less exhaustive, smaller deals with multiple production partners. How much this bungled deal relates to “XP,” a new cross-media dedicated department, is unconfirmed. It feels safe to assume it was constructed to pick up some of the slack.

As game development becomes outrageously costly and gaming itself prohibitively expensive, publishers big and small are seeking cross-media deals to double dip on their properties. HBOâs The Last of Us and Illuminationâs Super Mario movies have rallied audiences, often rerouting attention back to the source material. Giving existing back catalogues a second wind.

Itâs a phenomenon Xbox is plenty familiar with as well. Both Warner Bros.â Minecraft movie and Amazonâs Fallout show proved to be monumental hits. Not all cross-media expanses are made equally. Despite being the crown jewel of Xbox, Paramountâs Halo series failed to capture the zeitgeist as effectively as the studio’s Sega pursuits.

Itâs unclear which games Netflix was hoping to develop, but Microsoft literally has more games than they know what to do with. At the same time, itâs a big wide world. Doom, Elder Scrolls, Gears of War, Call of Duty, Space Quest. As big as Xboxâs tank is, there are ultimately plenty more fish in the sea for Netflix to cook with. As is Netflix has developed shows around Cyberpunk, League of Legends, The Witcher, Castlevania and streaming rights to the live-action Zelda next year.

articles.headline: The pros and cons of using an eSIM over a physical SIM card
keyFacts: An eSIM offers the same reception and data speed as a physical SIM card, but uses built-in hardware and downloadable profiles instead of a removable card.
The main advantages of an eSIM include flexibility, easy travel plan activation without a retailer, and storing multiple profiles for work and personal numbers.
The primary disadvantages of using an eSIM are device and carrier compatibility limits, and potential complications when transferring service between phones.
body: The pros and cons of using an eSIM over a physical SIM card
The conveniences of an eSIM come with a few strings attached.

First, you should know there is no quality difference between using an eSIM or physical SIM card. The difference between the two is how you activate and move your cellular service. Both identify your subscription to a mobile network and feature the same reception and data speed. A physical SIM is removable, while an eSIM uses built-in hardware and a downloadable carrier profile.

The primary advantages eSIM has over physical cards is that it's flexible and convenient. You don't have to open a side tray or transfer the SIM when you purchase a new phone. Instead, you can simply activate a supported plan via an app, QR code or the phone's settings. On compatible devices, you can even store multiple profiles, which makes it easier to separate your work and personal numbers without carrying around spare SIM cards.

If you spend a lot of time on the road, there's another useful eSIM feature to consider. With an unlocked, compatible phone, you can purchase a travel eSIM ahead of time instead of finding a retailer that sells physical SIMs once you reach your destination. Depending on your plan, that could save you some money instead of roaming with your home carrier. You can also keep the travel plan dormant on your phone until your next trip, compared to losing the SIM card at home. At the same time, an eSIM is not a guarantee of a better deal. For instance, some domestic cell plans already include international roaming, so switching is mostly a waste of time.

There are smaller pros too, like not having to wait on a SIM card to ship for a new plan. Plus, removing the SIM slot from phones broadly means manufacturers have more room for larger batteries or other improvements elsewhere.
Is there a downside to using eSIM?

There's always a drawback, and the biggest disadvantage of eSIM is compatibility and transferring service. Both the phone and carrier have to support eSIM, and that support may vary by model and the market. An eSIM also can't bypass a carrier lock; to use another provider's plan, your phone generally needs to be unlocked. Opera's free eSIM on Android is a good test before purchasing one.

Knowing that, it's always a good idea to look over the requirements before purchasing a travel plan or assuming you can move your existing number to a different device. After all, a downloadable profile is only useful if the phone and provider will activate it.

Some carriers make the business of moving service from one phone to another more complicated than it needs to be. With Apple's eSIM Quick Transfer, you can move service between compatible phones without contacting support, but some require a carrier app, a replacement QR code (as if we need more of those) or help from customer service. Fortunately, cross-platform transfers are improving. For instance, some iPhones and Android phones can now transfer eSIMs directly.

You also have to be careful with your carrier while traveling internationally, which means reading the fine print before you head out. For instance, you might still be able to utilize your normal phone number while using the travel plan for data, but your carrier may have hidden some roaming fees. Make sure your phone is set to use the travel eSIM for data upon your arrival. You can also turn off your regular line entirely, but you won't receive any cell calls or texts on that number while it's disabled.
Why are people against eSIM?

For some, the primary objection is losing the fallback simplicity of a physical SIM. For all the talk about switching from one phone to another with an eSIM, popping the tray open and physically switching a card to another phone is pretty easy, unless you have a severe case of fumble fingers. As previously stated, some carriers require in-app QR codes or switches, both of which can be a pain. So it's less about the convenience of an eSIM and more about the available tools and how efficient they are.

Physical SIMs still offer a wider degree of compatibility with older and simpler phones, which works out great for the Gen Zers going retro or the many seniors who still prefer them (though that's changing). While there's no removable card to lose or physically extract, digital activation doesn't eliminate account fraud or SIM-swap scams either.

Ultimately, it boils down to what "convenience" matters more to you. If your phone supports both formats, then you're good whichever way you go. In fact, you can do both: retaining your physical SIM while using an eSIM for another supported line.

articles.headline: Abelina is a strange, platforming romp through a natural afterlife from a former League of Legends animator and the composer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil
keyFacts: Abelina is a surreal platformer video game about a dead man named Vasily navigating a natural afterlife.
The game is led by former CG cinematic animator Gabe Askew with a soundtrack composed by Ryan Holladay.
The publisher states that Abelina is scheduled for release on Steam in the year 2027.
body: I have no particular thoughts on what the afterlife may look like, namely because if there is one, and I'm allowed to hang out in it, I don't want to be disappointed. What if I have the expectation that it's a hedonistic paradise and am met with only having a guy named Gary who only eats cheese sandwiches for company? How embarrassing! No, I'll leave the imagining to others on this particular front. Doing so bears some ripe fruit for me occasionally, too, as is the case today with Abelina, a surreal platformer about a man who died and finds himself tending to gardens and carving masks and trying "not to think about what this place might really be."

My immediate reaction upon seeing Abelina is that it has the vibe of a Soviet stop motion film only Letterboxd users have heard of, which is perhaps the highest compliment I can give to a game graphically. In it, you play as Vasily, who "died a while ago." He finds himself in the titular Abelina, an odd, nature-filled afterlife, where he's been trying to find happiness again with a small handful of other folks doing the same.

I don't think Abelina is a puzzle game, but it does look like you have to put some thought into your platforming at points. There is flying to be done, dungbeetle-esque rolling, precise jumps to be made. It seems the entire thing is about navigating this otherworldly locale, and hopefully finding some truth amongst it all. You may not always find the correct path, with branching paths and open vistas seemingly offering a multitude of ways forward, all while being led by a "mysterious rabbit-cat."

It's also a game with some skill behind it, being led by Gabe Askew, who's worked on CG cinematics for the likes of Valorant, League of Legends and Love, Death + Robots. Sonically we should be in for a pleasant time too, as Weapons and the recent Resident Evil movie's composer Ryan Holladay is on the soundtrack for Abelina. I'm curious about what else it has to offer and am keen to get my hands on it to see how that platforming feels. In the meantime, you might join me by wishlisting it on Steam ahead of its release in 2027.

articles.headline: Dalton Smith survives huge scare to retain world title and instantly calls out Shakur Stevenson
keyFacts: Dalton Smith defeated Alberto Puello by a split decision in Sheffield to retain his WBC super lightweight title.
Smith suffered a cut above his right eye and a split cheek during the gruelling 12-round bout.
Following his victory, Smith called out WBO champion Shakur Stevenson for a potential future fight.
body: Dalton Smith edged out a gruelling points victory over Alberto Puello to retain his WBC super lightweight title.
The 29-year-old won on a split decision, with England’s Kieran McCann and Spain’s Jon Llona scoring the fight 115-113 in his favour, with Filipino judge Ray Danseco having it 116-112 for Puello.
Smith retained his WBC strap in his first world title defence Getty
It was a return to his native Sheffield for Smith after he knocked out Subriel Matias in New York earlier this year to win the famous green and gold strap.
And in his first title defence, he fought Puello, who lost the WBC belt to Matias last year.
Smith was made to work for the victory, with the unbeaten Brit suffering a cut above his right eye and a split cheek in the 12th round.
But he did just enough to nick a points victory – setting up a potential mega fight in 2027.
Having told talkSPORT he believes he is one of the most underappreciated boxers , Smith is now ready to trade blows with WBO king Shakur Stevenson , who also holds the coveted Ring strap.
What did Dalton Smith say after beating Alberto Puello?
Speaking to DAZN, Smith said: “Boxing is business.
“I have a lot of respect for Shakur, he’s one hell of a fighter.
“But this takes me back to the Ricky Hatton-[Floyd] Mayweather days.
“And we could build something good, I have true respect for Shakur, he’s a great champion.”
His promoter Eddie Hearn then teased a potential unification bout, as he quipped: “I know Shakur Stevenson loves Sheffield in May.”
Smith was made to work for his points victory over Puello in Sheffield Getty
Commenting on his future plans, Smith also stated: “Number one goal in my life was to become world champion and make history, the second was to sell out Hillsborough stadium.
“I had that carrot dangled out in front of me for so long, I had to block out the noise, stay professional, it was hard, and keep my eyes on the ball tonight.”
Smith was also quick to heap praise on Puello, who also held the WBA belt between 2022-2023.
He remarked: “We knew what we were coming in for, he’s a two-time world champion [and] look at the names he’s beat.
“We knew it wasn’t going to be a show, he was going to be an awkward opponent, but a champion has to do what he has to do.
“These are the best in the world and I’m proving why I’m number one now.”

Before adding: “I got his rhythm early on, I think he respected my power, but look, he’s experienced.
“He’s a lot more experienced than me, and that’s what I’m gaining now.
“I switched off a little bit in the early rounds, but I did what a true champion did and win the last couple, so I’m very proud.”

articles.headline: Brazil’s Lula, Bolsonaro draw thousands to election-eve rallies
keyFacts: Brazilian presidential candidates Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro held final campaign rallies drawing thousands of supporters.
Lula is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term against senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.
Recent polling shows Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro remain about even ahead of Sunday's run-off election.
body: Brazil’s presidential candidates Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro have rallied thousands of supporters in a final show of campaign strength in advance of the country’s closely contested run-off election.

Donning a red hat, Lula addressed hundreds of supporters at Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach on Saturday, waving a Brazilian flag from a campaign truck as crowds gathered on the final day of campaigning.

“The people must choose either someone who kisses the national flag or someone who kisses the American flag”, the 80-year-old told the crowd as he referenced his opponent’s ties to US President Donald Trump.

Lula is seeking a fourth, non-consecutive term in Sunday’s run-off, which will task Brazilians with determining whether to stick with their incumbent left-wing leader or join a broader regional shift towards the right.
Bolsonaro, a senator and son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, secured 47 percent of the vote in the first round, narrowly ahead of Lula’s 45 percent.
Recent polling shows Lula and the younger Bolsonaro remain about even on the eve of the pivotal election.

A CNT/MDA survey released on Saturday revealed Bolsonaro would receive 46.3 percent of the vote compared with 45 percent for the left-wing Lula. Last week, the poll showed a slightly closer race with Bolsonaro leading Lula 46.8 percent to 45.9 percent.
The poll’s margin of error was 2.2 percentage points.
On Saturday, Bolsonaro’s supporters, including hundreds of motorcyclists wearing Brazil’s yellow national football shirts, gathered in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais.
One of those supporters, Ebert Dorigo, accused Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) of encouraging dependence on government welfare, arguing a change in direction was needed for the country.

“The values we uphold are nation and family. Our country is divided today because, due to welfare-based policies, some people … haven’t grasped that improvement and achievement come only through hard work,” he told the news agency AFP.

The bitter campaign has exposed deep divisions over economic policy, crime and Brazil’s political future, which Bolsonaro has pledged to tackle with hundreds of thousands of more spots in prison and cuts to government spending.
His father, who served as president from 2019 to 2022, is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after losing that year’s election to Lula.
The two candidates struck a calmer tone during their final debate on Friday, although they traded accusations over the country’s economic difficulties and their respective records.
For some voters, however, the choice has been a difficult one.

“If there were any other candidate, that would be a better option,” Gabriela Ribeiro Viana, an event organiser, told AFP. “But we’re stuck choosing between the worst, the horrible, and the lesser evil”.

articles.headline: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
keyFacts: BBC’s Blue Planet III is including imperfect shots with debris and poor conditions to prove its footage is authentic.
Executive Producer Elizabeth White said the production is keeping in elements that would normally be cut to counter the overly polished look of AI.
The series features remarkable animal behaviors, such as dolphins trapping fish and thousands of crabs feeding in formation.
body: BBC’s Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all.
Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real.

Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot. Or “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’” Instead, this time they’re leaving it all in to show a more authentic, organic version of the oceans.

The series features incredible displays of dolphins trapping fish by plugging holes with sea sponges, inter-species fish communication, and 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed. White says that real ocean creatures “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine.”

articles.headline: AG Tish James to hire outside lawyer to probe ‘Cornell 7’ after making prejudicial comments about case: sources
keyFacts: New York Attorney General Letitia James is hiring outside counsel to investigate seven Cornell fraternity brothers accused of rape after facing bias criticism.
Critics called for James to step aside, arguing her social media post supporting the alleged victim compromised the investigation's fairness.
The Attorney General's office is interviewing former federal prosecutors to lead and support the special prosecutor investigation.
body: Embattled New York Attorney General Letitia James is planning to hire outside counsel to investigate the seven Cornell University fraternity brothers accused of raping a female classmate — after coming under fire to recuse herself for making prejudicial comments about the incident, The Post has learned.
The AG’s office has already interviewed multiple former federal prosecutors to probe the “Cornell 7” case, and the leading candidates include powerhouse lawyer Maggie Gandy, sources said.

Gandy was deputy chief of the organized crime and gang section as a former Brooklyn federal prosecutor and is now a partner in the women-owned boutique firm Corva Law LLP, which specializes in civil rights, sexual misconduct matters, and criminal defense.
Alexis Richards, a spokesperson for attorney general, said the office was in the process of seeking outside counsel help “before” anyone said James “should be removed from the case.”
She also said she hasn’t “even heard” Gandy is a candidate, adding “you should not report that.”

“What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable,” the attorney general wrote on X on Sept. 28. “I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers. To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you.”
Critics – including President Trump — immediately called for her to step away, saying she was too political, biased and unethical to fairly investigate the case.

Norman Siegel, a longtime civil rights lawyer, said James is doing the right thing, adding that her taking the case would be like a police commissioner commenting on police misconduct cases before a probe is finished.
“These high profile cases have to be fair and unbiased,” the former New York Civil Liberties Union head said Saturday.
“People have to be extremely disciplined in what they say. The optics have to be 100% fair and unbiased.
“She tried to show empathy for the alleged victim,” he added. “I say ‘alleged.’ We don’t know all the facts. Some people have convicted the men in this case.
“It’s prudent for the attorney general to appoint an outside attorney to lead and assist the case at this point. It will address some of the optics that have been raised.”

Hochul erred in appointing James as a special prosecutor given the AG’s prior comments, and James should have recused herself or declined taking the case, said James Quinn, a former top prosecutor in the Queens District Attorney’s Office.
“It’s one mistake after another,” said Quinn, while adding that hiring an independent lawyer “is the only thing to do.”

Republican Saritha Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor trying to unseat James as attorney general in the Nov. 3 general election, said the AG’s decision to seek outside help shows James “is not qualified to prosecute this case and not qualified to be the attorney general of this state.”
“This turn of events underscores what we’ve been saying all along — what New York needs now is a prosecutor as attorney general,” she said.
Gandy and Hochul didn’t return messages on Saturday.

“On Thursday evening, after the Governor appointed the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) as a special prosecutor, Attorney General James and her team began a comprehensive investigation led by OAG’s Criminal Justice Division. Since then, OAG has spoken with the Tompkins County District Attorney, Jane Doe’s attorney, and several candidates for outside counsel to support the investigation,” an OAG spokesperson said in a statement. “The DA has agreed to cooperate, and OAG remains committed to a thorough and independent investigation guided only by the facts and the law.”
James campaign spokesperson Grace Smoker told The Post, “It’s unconscionable that Ms. Komatireddy would play politics with a sensitive criminal investigation.
“It doesn’t get any lower than that. Attorney General James is focused on following the facts and the law. Our opponent should try to do the same.”

The “Cornell 7” case became national news after a “Jane Doe” filed a lawsuit in Manhattan Supreme Court two months ago accusing seven fraternity brothers of raping her at Cornell’s Phi Chi fraternity house in October 2024.

articles.headline: Elon Musk says SpaceX throttled Ukraine Starlink speeds over drone strikes
keyFacts: Elon Musk said SpaceX throttled Ukraine's Starlink service after Ukraine used it for offensive drone strikes.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Starlink speeds have been restored to pre-restriction levels.
Russia agreed to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month.
body: Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.

Musk's admission on social media came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week.
Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.

"The speeds are now where they need to be," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that restoration began overnight and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving front-line logistics and defense against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
Musk admits he was behind Starlink's speed restriction

Before Musk's confirmation, questions persisted last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Ukraine has relied on for years to counter Moscow's attacks.
President Trump had said he didn't make the call, while also saying Musk should not be blamed. On Tuesday, CBS News reported that the disruption.
In a post Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX throttled the Starlink satellite internet service.

"Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote. "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."

But he maintained that the U.S. government controlled whatever changes happened with Starshield, SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service and the of Ukraine's drone operations and communication. He also defended the role of SpaceX in bolstering Ukraine's defenses since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Restrictions imposed last week on Starshield alarmed the country's military and government officials, with commanders reporting lost drones and disrupted missions.

The restoration follows a new U.S. diplomatic push to end the war. Russia agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month. On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow also agreed to a localized ceasefire brokered by first lady Melania Trump around Oleshky, a war-ravaged, Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's southern Kherson region.
The episode added to tensions between Kyiv and Washington, a relationship already strained by Mr. Trump's reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports, which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal.
Khmara credited "direct dialogue" and Zelenskyy's diplomacy with Washington, adding that the outcome mattered most "for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics and communications."
Zelenskyy on Saturday thanked Americans and "all our partners, who took all this seriously and are really helping us."

articles.headline: This cult classic edutainment game comes with an evil substitute teacher and a jumpscare ghost—and is the perfect fit for Halloween learning
keyFacts: Released in 1996, JumpStart Adventures 4th Grade: Haunted Island is a point-and-click educational game that combines spooky themes with math, reading, and social studies lessons.
Players must rescue their classmates from a witch substitute teacher named Mrs. Grunkle by completing educational minigames and collecting keys on a haunted island.
The game features unsettling environments and a persistent ghost named Repsac who ambushes players with random trivia questions.
body: The JumpStart Adventures series may as well be the royal family of educational games. These titles found some pretty wild ways to make learning fun and engaging, but only one is a soft survival-horror piece.

1996’s JumpStart Adventures 4th Grade: Haunted Island isn’t just an educational game with spooky elements; it’s a full-on point-and-click adventure that delivers genuine chills while giving its intended audience a surprisingly fun crash course in math, social studies, and reading.

Image via Knowledge Adventure JumpStart Adventures games are usually story-driven, and 4th Grade: Haunted Islands has one of the best in the series. Players step into the shoes of an average fourth-grader who sets out to save their classmates from Mrs. Grunkle, a witch moonlighting as a substitute teacher who transformed the entire class (sans an absent player) into monsters before whisking them away to the titular island.

4th Grade: Haunted Island ‘s gameplay blends exploration with traditional educational-game shenanigans. Under the guidance of soothsayer Madame Pomreeda (yes, you read that right), players traverse the island and recover their classmates’ lost possessions, which are required to change them back into humans. Naturally, you earn these possessions by completing minigames that test your math, reading comprehension, and social studies skills.

Turning the classmates back to normal is only part of the mission, though. Players also need to collect the 25 keys to Mrs. Grunkles’ house before they can actually save the kids. Scoring high on minigames unlocks keys, subtly encouraging players to internalize what the game teaches them, improve their scores, and make progress. It’s a surprisingly effective gameplay loop that makes learning fun, which I’ll argue is the ultimate goal of every educational game.
Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !

While 4th Grade: Haunted Island ‘s educational side is pretty solid, it really shines in delivering on the spook promised by its title. With its Tim Burton-influenced character design, theremin-dominated soundtrack, and surprisingly detailed environments for its time, the game absolutely nails the Halloween vibe it’s going for.

The game can even be genuinely unsettling at points. One area you need to progress through is a forest of trees with monstrous expressions etched into their trunks, and the low-angle first-person perspective really heightens the experience. The cemetery section asks the player to read some pretty intense scary stories, some of which feel like they belong in a Goosebumps book. But these haunts are nothing, nothing at all, compared to Repsac.

Image via Knowledge Adventure Repsac, Mrs. Grunkles’ right-hand specter, is a certified menace. This grinning ghoul follows you throughout the entire game, ambushing you with trivia questions whenever and wherever he feels like. Nowhere is safe from this guy, and the paranoia that builds as you wait for him to pop up is genuinely spine-chilling. In Reddit posts dedicated to 4th Grade: Haunted Island , Repsac and his pop-quiz habit come up pretty often.

That said, while the game packs a spooky punch, it never crosses the line into outright horror. The innate sense of play present in all the other JumpStart Adventures is alive and well here, and it keeps things from getting too grim. Kids love a good scare once in a while, and if the JumpStart fandom’s opinion of this game is any indication, many who played it had a great time.

Educational games have become a lost art in modern gaming, but if you’re in the mood to relive the glory days of PC edutainment this Halloween (or know a younger gamer who never experienced this era of gaming), 4th Grade: Haunted Island could be a great way to spend an evening or two. Emulation websites like My Abandonware host the game’s files and provide instructions for downloading them safely online. Just remember to be careful; old game files can be unstable.
The post This cult classic edutainment game comes with an evil substitute teacher and a jumpscare ghost—and is the perfect fit for Halloween learning appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
keyFacts: Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara stated that SpaceX's Starshield system appears to be working normally again for the Ukrainian military.
The development followed a 10-day period of connectivity issues that caused Ukrainian drones to lose internet access at high speeds, according to reports.
President Donald Trump reportedly asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday to restore the Starshield service.
body: SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions the Ukrainian military’s of use Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions.

This follows a 10-day period where Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly.

President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, with Musk recently posting, “Zelensky has gone too far.”

The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.”
“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

articles.headline: Second Amendment fight moves beyond guns with Supreme Court poised for big ruling
keyFacts: Two federal courts ruled that Second Amendment protections extend to switchblade knives and body armor as protected arms.
The Supreme Court is preparing to hear oral arguments in Viramontes v. Cook County regarding AR-15-style rifle bans.
Dudley Brown said a Supreme Court ruling against AR-15 bans could influence future challenges to defensive equipment restrictions.
body: Two federal court rulings Wednesday extending Second Amendment protections to switchblade knives and body armor have fueled optimism among gun-rights advocates ahead of a major Supreme Court showdown over bans on AR-15-style rifles.

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that a federal law restricting the interstate commerce of switchblade knives violated the Second Amendment , while a federal judge in the Western District of New York struck down New York’s restrictions on personal body armor. In both cases, the courts determined that switchblades and body armor qualify as constitutionally protected "arms."

The twin rulings come as the Supreme Court prepares to hear oral arguments in Viramontes v. Cook County, a case that could determine whether AR-15-style rifles qualify as "arms" protected by the Second Amendment.

National Association for Gun Rights President Dudley Brown, whose organization filed an amicus brief in Viramontes, said a Supreme Court ruling against AR-15 bans could influence future legal challenges to restrictions on ammunition magazines , automatic knives, body armor and other defensive equipment.
"The interesting thing about both of these cases is that they’re both going to be really decided by the U.S. Supreme Court in the Viramontes decision," Brown told Fox News Digital.
SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY LIMITS USE OF GUN LAW USED TO PROSECUTE HUNTER BIDEN

The recent rulings rely on two major Supreme Court decisions defining the scope of the Second Amendment: District of Columbia v. Heller and New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen — both of which will play a key role in the Supreme Court’s review of AR-15-style rifle bans.

In its 2008 decision in Heller, the Supreme Court established that the Second Amendment protects an individual right to possess firearms for lawful purposes, including self-defense. The Court also ruled that the amendment protects weapons in lawful common use while acknowledging a longstanding tradition of restricting "dangerous and unusual" weapons.

Heller recognized that the term "arms" encompasses both offensive weapons and defensive armor. The decision did not address switchblades or body armor directly but the recent rulings relied on its broader understanding of what may qualify as an arm.
The decisions also reveal how Bruen ’s text-and-history test could shape the Supreme Court’s review of bans on AR-15-style rifles.

Under Bruen, courts first determine whether the Second Amendment’s text covers the weapon or conduct at issue. Because both courts answered that question affirmatively, the burden shifted to the governments to show that the restrictions were consistent with the nation’s historical tradition of arms regulation.
George Lyon, a Second Amendment attorney, said the governments in both cases failed to identify sufficiently similar historical laws justifying the modern restrictions.
ATF SUSPENDS FEDERAL REGISTRATION AND APPROVAL RULES FOR CERTAIN FIREARMS
"Once what you want to do is shown to come within the text of the Second Amendment, the presumption is that the regulation is unconstitutional," Lyon said.

The Fifth Circuit found that switchblades are commonly used "arms" protected by the Second Amendment, citing their historical use for defense and everyday purposes. It then ruled that the government had failed to identify a sufficient historical tradition for the Federal Switchblade Act ’s specific restrictions on interstate commerce, which regulated switchblades in a way that differed from historical laws.

In the New York ruling, the state argued that body armor was a tactical accessory to a firearm rather than an "arm" protected by the Second Amendment. The judge rejected that argument, finding that body armor falls within the historical definition of arms recognized in Heller. The court then concluded that New York had not shown a sufficient historical tradition supporting its civilian purchase ban.
That reasoning could become important in Viramontes, where the Supreme Court is being asked to decide whether AR-15-style rifles fall within the definition of protected arms recognized in Heller.
GUN RIGHTS GROUPS CAPITALIZE AFTER JUDGE REVERSES DECADES-OLD RESTRICTIONS: 'MONUMENTAL'

The case arises from a challenge to Cook County’s assault-weapons ban . The Seventh Circuit concluded that AR-15-style rifles were comparable to machine guns and therefore fell outside the category of arms protected by the Second Amendment. The Supreme Court’s decision could resolve whether that reasoning is consistent with Heller and Bruen.
Lyon said the Seventh Circuit improperly treated AR-15-style rifles as comparable to machine guns.

"The current case at the Supreme Court, Viramontes, will address that because the Seventh Circuit had taken the position that because AR-15s are ‘like machine guns,’ they don’t constitute an arm as defined under Heller," Lyon said. "That was just totally wrong in my view."

Justin Davis, director of public affairs for the National Rifle Association, said the dispute over AR-15-style rifles is part of a broader legal fight over what qualifies as an "arm" under the Second Amendment.
"There’s a major discussion going on in the courts about what is and what aren’t arms," Davis said.
Davis pointed to litigation involving suppressors, ammunition magazines, stun guns, pepper spray and other equipment used for self-defense.

"They talk about how the Second Amendment only applied to muskets because that’s what existed at the time of the Founders, but we don’t apply the First Amendment only to newspapers, books or speech in public forums," Davis said. "Social media, texting and phones didn’t exist at that time, either."
"The world evolves, but the core fundamental rights never change," Davis continued.

articles.headline: Top Xbox exec promoted in brand 'reset' leaves after 3 months in role
keyFacts: Xbox Chief Operating Officer Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after three months in the newly created role, according to an internal memo.
CEO Asha Sharma announced the departure without providing an explanation, while an anonymous source told Eurogamer that Chiang was terminated for policy violations.
Chiang's immediate responsibilities are being divided among other Xbox leaders until further leadership plans are finalized.
body: As reported by The Verge, Xbox Chief Operating Officer Helen Chiang is leaving the company after three months in the role—though Chiang had previously been a Microsoft employee for 21 years. Xbox had not previously operated with a COO in its hierarchy, and the role was created as part of CEO Asha Sharma's controversial brand "reset."

Sharma announced the personnel change in an October 23 internal memo, and did not offer an explanation for Chiang's departure. "Her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now," Sharma wrote. "We'll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized."

Microsoft shared a boilerplate statement on the departure to Eurogamer: "We don't discuss individual personnel matters. We're grateful for Helen's years of service and wish her well." However, an anonymous source within Microsoft also told Eurogamer that Chiang was "terminated for policy violations."

According to Sharma's original reset announcement, the COO was tasked "with end-to-end P&L [profit and loss] responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services." Given Xbox's current focus on cost-cutting and maximizing revenue, that sounds like a fairly key role in Sharma's project.

It's hard to imagine Chiang's departure having any significant impact on Xbox's strategy or its execution, but it hardly inspires confidence to see such a quick turnaround in an executive-level position, particularly given the overall instability and uncertainty at Xbox.

articles.headline: Man Destroys $2,000 iPhone Duo With Dirt, Fire, Knives and Medieval Chainmail
keyFacts: Tech reviewer Zach Nelson published a video testing the durability of Apple's new $2,000 foldable iPhone Duo.
Nelson subjected the device to scratch tests, dirt, medieval chainmail, and backward bending, which caused the main screen to crack.
CNET senior technology reporter Abrar Al-Heeti recommended getting a case and AppleCare to protect the device.
body: It might seem obvious, but try not to sit on your iPhone Duo when you leave it open.

That lesson comes a day after Apple’s foldable iPhone hit stores with lines of people queued up to buy the new device. Tech reviewer Zach Nelson dropped an iPhone Duo video on his YouTube channel, JerryRigEverything, testing the scratch resistance and bendability of the new $2,000 phone.
Let’s just say that Nelson’s measured, soothing voice didn’t keep me calm as he meticulously destroyed the Duo.
More from CNET

He subjected it to numerous scratch tests on both its cover and inner screens. Nelson praised Apple for the cover screen’s Ceramic Shield 2 glass and noted that the inner screen, even with its nano-texture finish, scratches as easily as the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s nonmatte folding display.
But why stop there?

Nelson used medieval chainmail (no proof it was actually from the Middle Ages), dirt, dust and pebbles to test the Duo further. Surprisingly, the new phone handled the chainmail easily. Nelson partly credits that to the Duo’s matte finish on the inner screen, which seems to hide imperfections.

He then opened the Duo’s inner screen and tried to bend it backward a few times. As you might expect, the frame flexed, which led to cracks showing up on the main 7.6-inch screen. So if you set your Duo down with its main screen open on a chair or couch, just don’t sit on it.

In a review by CNET senior technology reporter Abrar Al-Heeti, Al-Heeti recommends protecting the Duo, saying, “You should probably still get a case and AppleCare, or be prepared to pay a pretty penny for repairs.”

You can watch Nelson’s video to see the entire nearly 15-minute video. Warning: the dust and dirt portion against the Duo’s hinge is psychologically difficult to witness (because of all the dust and dirt). Also, if you’re wondering more about the iPhone Duo’s durability, CNET has designed and constructed a custom machine called the Fold-a-Phone that is currently hard at work testing how many times Apple’s foldable can be open and closed.
